facts.statement: Meterchen was described by Tennyson and colleagues.
Meterchen lived during the Miocene epoch.
The type locality for Meterchen is the Bannockburn Formation.
Fossils of Meterchen were found in New Zealand.
Meterchen is considered a probable goose.
Meterchen is a newly described genus and species.
Meterchen is currently considered a valid taxon.
The type species of the genus Meterchen is M. luti.
facts.quote: The type species is M. luti.

facts.statement: The only known species of Meterchen is Meterchen luti.
Meterchen luti was named by Tennyson et al. in 2026.
The name references the Mother Goose nursery rhyme about a goose rising from the mud.
facts.quote: The binomen therefore references the Mother Goose nursery rhyme where a mother goose rises up out of the mud.

facts.statement: The study describing Meterchen lists Alan J. D. Tennyson, Elizabeth M. Steell, Pascale Lubbe, Amy L. Adams, Liam Greer, Alex H. Brown, Laura J. E. Wilson, Timothy C. Campbell, Tobia C. Dale, and Nicolas J. Rawlence as authors.
facts.quote: Authors: Alan J. D. Tennyson, Elizabeth M. Steell, Pascale Lubbe, Amy L. Adams, Liam Greer, Alex H. Brown, Laura J. E. Wilson, Timothy C. Campbell, Tobia C. Dale, Nicolas J. Rawlence

facts.statement: The description of Meterchen was published in the journal Historical Biology.
Fossil records of Meterchen come from the Miocene St Bathans deposits in New Zealand.
